fullDescription.text: An anonymous attacker downloads the RSA public key from the browsable /encryptionkeys directory (server.ts:277-278), signs a JWT with HS256 using that public key as the HMAC secret (or sends alg none), and presents it to any route guarded by isAuthorized(). express-jwt 0.1.3 with jsonwebtoken 0.4.0 (package.json:112,132) verifies with `secret: publicKey` and no `algorithms` option, so the forged token with role admin and any victim id is accepted.

shortDescription.text: No formal approval workflow exists in the product review system.

fullDescription.text: No formal approval workflow exists in the product review system. The updateProductReviews route (PATCH /rest/products/reviews) allows any authenticated user to edit any review without ownership check, and existing likes are not reset after an edit — the closest analog to 'change content after approval and keep the earlier approval.' However, whether this constitutes a required approval boundary violation depends on the open question 'Does the process require separation between requester and approver?', which the code cannot resolve. Self-liking of reviews (likeProductReviews.ts line 31 checks only for duplicate likes, not self-likes) is also unrestricted, but 'liking' is not a formal approval gate. Cited operation has no ownership guard.

shortDescription.text: Role-gated operations (isAccounting, isDeluxe) read the role directly from the JWT payload without re-checking the database.

fullDescription.text: Role-gated operations (isAccounting, isDeluxe) read the role directly from the JWT payload without re-checking the database. The authenticatedUsers store has no delete/revoke operation, and the updateAuthenticatedUsers middleware re-adds any valid JWT automatically.
